decisions.statement: A wall time is resolved against the offset the candidate instant lands in.
A time said with a date is that Mountain wall time on that date.
Whether a time names a day of its own is answered here.
A timestamp closing in Z or in an offset is the instant that timestamp states.
Seconds a caller writes are kept.
An instant is handed back as UTC.
A wall time whose hour is 1 to 12 is read on a twelve hour clock.
A wall time whose hour is 0 or 13 to 23 is read on a twenty-four hour clock.
A twelve hour reading answers to an instant and to the instant twelve hours away.
A twenty-four hour reading answers to an instant a day.
A reading is looked for from one hour after now back as far as that reading repeats in.
The earliest instant a window reaches falls outside that window.
The latest instant a window reaches falls inside that window.
A window no clock turned inside has one reading.
A twelve hour window on the spring turn day can have two readings.
A twelve hour window on the autumn turn day can have no reading.
A window with more than one reading is refused.
A window with no reading is refused.
A wall time the clock skipped is refused.
A wall time the clock struck twice is refused.
A refusal asks for the date and the time to be said instead.
A day the calendar does not have is refused.
An hour past 23 or a minute past 59 is refused.
A time that will not read is handed back as a refusal.
Nothing here throws.
Nothing here reads a clock.
Now is handed in.
No clock but Denver's is read here.

definition: the instant a Mountain wall time names, and the time a Mountain clock reads at one
